messages.author: 5ea25187985f565f
messages.subject: Error Only When Using 1s Epochs
parts:
Hi Vincent,

Some of the recent updates to the GGIR package seem to have fixed most of the problems I was having before. There are still a couple I'm working on.
One new problem, which i'm hoping other users might be able to help with, is with "windowsizes". When I use the default windowsize (5,900,3600) the code runs as expected. However, if I change the window size to (1,900,3600) I get the following error (at the beginning of part 2):

Error in data.frame(r1 = r1, r2 = r2, r3 = r3, r4 = r4, r5 = r5) : 
  arguments imply differing number of rows: 860, 3600 In addition: Warning message:
In r1 + r2 + r3 + r4 :
  longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length

This occurs even when I am starting from scratch (i.e., including completing part 1 again). I wonder if anyone has encountered this problem before?

Many thanks,
Taren

messages.author: 8d92e34685fbc6bd
messages.subject: Re: [GGIR] Error Only When Using 1s Epochs
parts:
Hi Taren,
The error message you get sounds to me as if the code still is trying to process part2 with 1 second epochs based on part 1 output with 5 second epochs.

I see you make multiple calls to g.shell.GGIR to run the different parts of the pipeline, which introduces a chance for accidental inconsistencies in function arguments... I cannot spot any inconsistencies but it is possible given the large amount of arguments there are. Further, I see you move the data to a different location, which introduces the risk of forgetting that old data still sits somewhere.

For testing purposes, have you tried simplifying the procedure by making only a single call to g.shell.GGIR with mode = c(1,2) to run part 1 and 2 sequentially? Preferably with a clean output folder to avoid confusion about which files are being processed and which output to look at.

Best,Vincent
